ai.literal: The desire axe will break the self-control called modesty bolt fastened door.
ai.translation: The axe of desire will break open the door of self-control, which is secured by the bolt of modesty.
ai.modern: காமம் என்னும் கோடரி, நாணம் என்னும் தாழ்ப்பாள் போடப்பட்ட நிறை என்னும் கதவை உடைத்துவிடும்.
ai.explanation: The speaker expresses how overwhelming desire destroys her self-restraint. She compares her self-control to a locked door and her sense of modesty to the bolt that secures it. However, her intense passion acts like a heavy axe that easily shatters both the door and its bolt. The imagery vividly captures the helplessness of a lover whose inner defenses are broken by the sheer force of desire.

ai.literal: Love saying one-thing-alas mercy is-without; my heart at-midnight-even ruling action.
ai.translation: This thing called love has no mercy; its only work is to rule my heart even at midnight.
ai.modern: காமம் என்று சொல்லப்படும் ஒன்றுக்குக் கருணையே இல்லை; நள்ளிரவிலும் அது என் நெஞ்சத்தை ஆளும் செயலைக் கொண்டுள்ளது.
ai.explanation: The speaker laments the relentless nature of her love and longing. She notes that the affliction called love lacks any mercy or consideration for her suffering. Its sole occupation is to dominate and torment her heart unceasingly, keeping her awake and restless even during the dead of night when all else rests.

ai.literal: I will hide, indeed, the desire, I (alas)! Warning without, sneeze like, having appeared it will.
ai.translation: I try to hide my desire, but alas! Like a sneeze, it bursts forth without any warning.
ai.modern: நான் என் காமத்தை மறைக்கவே முயல்கிறேன்; ஆனால் அது எந்த முன்னறிவிப்பும் இல்லாமல் ஒரு தும்மலைப் போலத் தானாகவே வெளிப்பட்டு விடுகிறது.
ai.explanation: The speaker laments her inability to conceal her love and desire. She compares her passion to a sneeze, which is a sudden, involuntary reflex that cannot be suppressed. The word 'குறிப்பு' here means a warning or prior indication, showing that her emotions reveal themselves without giving her a chance to hold them back. The particle 'மன்' expresses her frustration and helplessness in trying to maintain her modesty.

ai.literal: Self-control possess-I say-will-I alas I-[emphasis] my passion secrecy having-crossed public-assembly will-appear
ai.translation: I used to say, 'I possess self-control.' But alas, my passion breaks out of its secrecy and appears in public.
ai.modern: நான் நிறையுடையவள் என்று சொல்வேன். ஆனால் என் காமமோ, தனக்குரிய மறைவிடத்தை விட்டு வெளியேறி, ஊரார் அறியும்படி மன்றத்தில் வெளிப்பட்டு நிற்கிறது.
ai.explanation: The speaker laments her inability to hide her love. She used to confidently claim that she had the inner strength and reserve (niṟai) to keep her feelings hidden. However, her passion (kāmam) has grown so strong that it breaks past all secrecy (maṟai) and exposes itself in the public square (maṉṟu). The contrast between her past confidence and her present exposure highlights the overwhelming power of love.

ai.literal: After those who scorned not going great dignity love-disease afflicted those knowing one thing is not.
ai.translation: The noble pride of not pursuing those who have scorned us is not a thing known to those afflicted by the disease of love.
ai.modern: நம்மை வெறுத்துச் சென்றவர் பின்னே செல்லாத பெருமை, காம நோயால் துன்பப்படுபவர்கள் அறியும் ஒரு செயல் அல்ல.
ai.explanation: The speaker reflects on the loss of her self-control and dignity. Normally, a person of great dignity would never chase after someone who has scorned or abandoned them. However, this noble pride is completely unknown to those suffering from the intense affliction of love, compelling her to seek out her lover despite his neglect.

ai.literal: Those who spurned behind going desiring pitiful alas of what nature me struck sorrow
ai.translation: Alas, how pitiful is this sorrow that has struck me! It makes me want to go after the very person who spurned me.
ai.modern: என்னை விட்டுப் பிரிந்தவர் பின்னால் செல்லும்படி தூண்டுகின்ற என் துயரம் எத்தன்மைத்து! இது மிகவும் இரங்கத்தக்கது.
ai.explanation: The heroine laments the overwhelming nature of her lovesickness, which destroys her modesty and pride. Even though her lover has left her, her sorrow pushes her to abandon her dignity and go after him. The word 'அளித்து' highlights the pitiful state of her heart, while 'எற்று' questions the strange, compelling nature of this grief.

ai.literal: modesty called even one thing we do not know, by passion he who cares pleasingly if does.
ai.translation: I know nothing of a thing called modesty when my lover, out of passion, does exactly what pleases me.
ai.modern: காதலர் தன் காமத்தால் நான் விரும்பும் செயல்களைச் செய்தால், நாணம் என்று சொல்லப்படும் ஒரு பொருளை நான் அறிய மாட்டேன்.
ai.explanation: The heroine expresses how her deep love overcomes her natural sense of reserve. She states that if her lover acts out of passion to do exactly what pleases her ('பெட்ப செயின்'), she completely loses herself. In those moments, she does not even recognize a concept called modesty ('நாண் என ஒன்றோ அறியலம்'). The word 'பேணியார்' refers to the lover who cares for her, highlighting that his affectionate actions dissolve her inhibitions.

ai.literal: Of many tricks thief's humble words are they not our womanhood breaking weapon
ai.translation: Are not the submissive words of that rogue of many tricks the very weapon that shatters my feminine reserve?
ai.modern: பல மாயங்களைச் செய்யும் கள்வனாகிய என் காதலனின் பணிவான வார்த்தைகள் என்னுடைய பெண்மை என்னும் உறுதியை உடைக்கும் ஆயுதமாக இருக்கின்றன அல்லவா?
ai.explanation: The heroine admits to her friend that she cannot maintain her feminine reserve and stay angry at her lover. She calls him a thief of many tricks because he knows exactly how to deceive her heart. His humble, pleading words act as a powerful weapon that effortlessly shatters her steadfastness and modesty.

ai.literal: "I will sulk" saying I went; I embraced, heart mingling about to experience having seen.
ai.translation: I went to him thinking, "I will sulk," but seeing my heart rushing to unite with him, I embraced him instead.
ai.modern: "நான் அவரிடம் பிணங்குவேன்" என்று நினைத்துக்கொண்டு சென்றேன்; ஆனால் என் நெஞ்சம் அவரோடு கலக்க முற்படுவதைக் கண்டு, பிணங்குவதை விட்டு அவரைத் தழுவிக்கொண்டேன்.
ai.explanation: The speaker describes her failed attempt to maintain her reserve and feign anger with her lover. She approaches him with the firm intention to sulk. However, before she can act cold, she realizes her own heart is already rushing to unite with him. Betrayed by her own heart's eagerness, she abandons her pride and embraces him. The contrast between her planned action and her actual action highlights the overpowering nature of love over self-control.

ai.literal: fat in-fire like-having-put to-those-with-heart is-there having-united having-feigned-anger we-will-stand saying
ai.translation: Can those whose hearts melt like fat thrown into fire say, "We will stand firm in our feigned anger when we are together"?
ai.modern: தீயில் இட்ட கொழுப்பைப் போல உருகும் நெஞ்சத்தை உடையவர்களுக்கு, காதலருடன் சேர்ந்திருக்கும்போது ஊடல் கொண்டு நிற்போம் என்று சொல்வது முடியுமோ?
ai.explanation: The heroine reflects on her inability to maintain her feigned anger (ஊடல்) when she is with her lover. She compares her heart to fat (நிணம்) thrown into a fire, which melts instantly and completely. For someone whose heart melts so easily out of love, it is impossible to resolve to stand firm in feigned anger. The vivid imagery of fat melting in fire perfectly captures how her resolve dissolves in his presence.
